transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-23
Start: 14:30 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Samir Gupta (Redwood SE), Aisha Rahman (NimbusCart Head of Search), Ben Torres (NimbusCart Staff ML Eng), Claire Wu (NimbusCart CTO)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): NimbusCart is evaluating Redwood for an embeddings+rerank pipeline for product search. Primary constraints: sub-200ms p95 for rerank path, cost targets for 10k QPS embedding fanout, and PCI/data residency constraints pushing toward private VPC or dedicated. Agreed to run a 1M-vector throughput/latency benchmark and exchange security docs.

Topics: hosting, VPC, quantization, dimensioning, hybrid search, vector DB choices, reranker model placement

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros and then we want to understand your current stack and success criteria.
[00:12] Aisha: Hi, Aisha here. We own search at NimbusCart. We're in the middle of redoing the ranking stack, want embeddings + rerank for product similarity and query expansion.
[00:21] Ben: Ben here, I run the feature infra and embed pipelines. We're using a homegrown FAISS cluster today with CPU-only pods, and we've been hitting throughput/latency issues.
[00:32] Claire: Claire, CTO. High-level: security/compliance is important; some payment-related data needs to stay in our VPC.
[00:39] Jordan: Great. Samir from Redwood will do the infra deep dive. Samir, over to you.
[00:45] Samir: Thanks. Quick Qs: what's your QPS distribution per endpoint, tail requirements, and how big are embeddings (dim)?
[00:53] Ben: Good question. Two main flows: synchronous search queries (about 6k QPS peak, median 2k) that fan out to top-k retrieval; and async batch indexing. Embedding dim: currently 1536 for our model, but we're exploring 768/512 to reduce cost.
[01:12] Samir: OK. For 6k QPS with a fanout of 50 candidates and then a rerank, the serving topology matters — you can either run embedding search in a vector DB (we've seen customers use Pinecone/Milvus) and then call a lightweight reranker in Redwood, or embed-and-index with an in-model rerank co-located on dedicated infra. What SLOs on rerank latency?
[01:31] Aisha: P95 ideally under 200ms end-to-end for the rerank path. We can tolerate higher for some tail cases but want predictable cost.
[01:40] Samir: Understood. Two patterns to consider: 1) hybrid search: vector DB does the recall, then Redwood hosted/dedicated runs a small 2-3 layer reranker (quantized t5-ish) for top 10. That minimizes model ops but adds a cross-network hop. 2) co-locate the reranker in the same private cluster (dedicated or private, maybe on-prem) to save rtt for p95. Tradeoffs: cost vs predictable latency.
[02:05] Ben: Network hop is the worry — our current tail is spiky because some hosts are overloaded. If we go hosted, how do you handle burst spikes?
[02:15] Jordan: We have reserved dedicated pools for predictable throughput (Redwood Dedicated) and hosted auto-scaling for variable workloads. For bursts, we offer burst capacity and burst routing to alternate regions/models. Also caching (prefix/KV cache) helps repeated queries.
[02:29] Ben: That KV cash — sorry, cache — is that persisted per-tenant or ephemeral?
[02:33] Samir: It's per-tenant by default, persists to customer namespace with TTLs. It can save a lot of work on repeated prefixes. But for first-pass retrieval you still need vector fanout.
[02:44] Aisha: On the vector DB side, we currently maintain FAISS shards. We're exploring managed vector DBs — Pinecone and Milvus popped up. How does Redwood integrate? Does Redwood do the fanout, or do you expect the vector DB to return candidates?
[02:58] Samir: Both patterns are supported. Typical approach: vector DB returns candidate ids with scores (recall), then Redwood does rerank. Alternatively, some customers choose embed-in-index and serve directly from the Redwood runtime using an index sharded across GPUs — that's more common on Dedicated/Private. The former is simpler with existing vector DBs.
[03:16] Ben: If we keep our Milvus cluster, can we avoid double-serving and extra egress costs?
[03:22] Samir: Yes — you can keep Milvus, and we only call it for recall. Egress costs depend on your cloud region and VPC peering. If you go Private (VPC), traffic stays internal and egress is lower.
[03:32] Claire: PCI/regulatory teams want the model never see raw payment identifiers. We need to know data retention and how logs are stored.
[03:39] Samir: We'll share SOC2 and our data residency whitepaper. For Private deployments, the control plane can be customer-managed and logs forwarded to your SIEM. We'll include the logs retention options in the security doc.
[03:52] Jordan: Back to throughput: Ben, can you share typical vector sizes and index size?
[03:57] Ben: We've got ~2.3M products currently; target pilot will use 1M subset. Dim is 1536 originally but we want to test 768 and 512 quantized to int8.
[04:08] Samir: Good. For 1M at 768 with int8 quant, memory footprint and KV cache hit improve. Computationally, 6k QPS fanout 50 -> 300k distance ops/sec. On GPU-backed Dedicated with optimized kernels you can handle that with sharding and batching; on hosted you rely on dynamic batching + consistent routing.
[04:28] Aisha: How do you recommend we set up reranker size? We don't want a huge 11B model if it's only for top 10 rerank.
[04:35] Samir: Right — many customers use a compact reranker (e.g., 1.3B quantized) or distilled T5 for rerank. You can A/B with a stronger model for a fraction of traffic. Redwood Optimize suggests quantization profiles per workload.
[04:47] Ben: Any sample numbers for p95 on a co-located reranker vs hosted remote?
[04:51] Samir: Roughly, co-located on Dedicated: p95 rerank ~40-80ms for top10 with a 1.3B quantized model depending on batching. Hosted remote (cross-region) may add 80-150ms network, pushing p95 higher. These are ballpark — we'll run the benchmark.
[05:07] Jordan: Also worth calling out fallback policies: if the dedicated pool is saturated we can failover to a smaller hosted model automatically. That can help availability.
[05:16] Claire: Cost — our finance team wants $/query under $0.01 for this path at scale. Is that realistic?
[05:22] Jordan: Depends on model, batch sizes, and embedding dims. Quantization and batching reduce token/compute cost. For a top10 rerank with a small model and int8 embeddings on Dedicated with high utilization, customers see sub-cent per query in some cases. We'll need to run numbers against your distribution.
[05:36] Ben: Ok, assume pilot with 1M vectors, 768 dims, quantized. Our QPS for pilot will be 2k steady with spikes to 6k.
[05:45] Samir: Good test plan. We'll set up a benchmark harness to replay your QPS distribution and test both architectures: (A) Milvus recall + Redwood hosted rerank, (B) Dedicated co-located rerank and possibly embed-in-index.
[05:58] Aisha: For the benchmark, what do you need from us?
[06:02] Samir: Sample dataset (1M vectors subset), expected QPS trace (CSV with timestamps QPS), target SLOs, plus access details for your Milvus endpoint if we are to integrate into the test. Ben, can you provide that?
[06:13] Ben: Yes, I can. I will also provide current query distribution and typical query latencies.
[06:18] Jordan: We'll produce a pricing estimate for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private including reserved capacity options and burst policies.
[06:25] Claire: Regarding private deployment, what's the upgrade and support model? We want to avoid long maintenance windows.
[06:31] Samir: For Private deployments we do a managed control plane; you own the VPC and we push updates through a customer-approved pipeline. Support SLAs are configurable; we can offer Enterprise support for 24/7, plus runbook handoffs.
[06:44] Ben: One more thing — embedding dim reduction will change accuracy. Would you recommend we do a fidelity sweep?
[06:50] Samir: Yes. Redwood Optimize can run a sweep: evaluate 1536 vs 768 vs 512 on a hold-out set measuring recall@k and rerank lift. We'll tie regressions to alerts.
[07:00] Aisha: Great. Also curious on model version pinning and rollouts — we need safe canaries for rerank changes.
[07:06] Samir: Rollouts are supported — you can do canary traffic splits, A/B tests, automatic rollbacks if quality dips. We also provide eval hooks to run prompt sets or rerank test sets pre-deploy.
[07:17] Jordan: Any competitors you're looking at?
[07:19] Claire: Mainly Pinecone for vector DB + custom rerank, and evaluating Cohere/Anthropic for model endpoints. We're open.
[07:27] Samir: Noted. We'll show integration patterns and pros/cons in the follow-up doc.
[07:33] (brief crosstalk)
[07:40] Ben: Operational question: if we do Dedicated, how do we handle scaling down at night? We don't want idle GPUs burning cost.
[07:48] Samir: Dedicated supports configurable autoscale policies and scheduled scale-downs; you can also mix reserved baseline capacity plus burst to hosted to cover spikes and reduce idle cost.
[07:58] Aisha: For logging and audit trails, does Redwood push logs to customer SIEM or store in Redwood?
[08:03] Samir: Both. For Hosted, logs are retained per account, and we can forward to your SIEM via secure syslog/forwarder. For Private, logs remain in your VPC.
[08:12] Jordan: Let's recap next steps so everyone is aligned.
[08:16] Jordan: Action items: Jordan to send pricing/options and high-level architecture doc; Samir to send SOC2 excerpt and benchmarking plan; Ben to provide dataset and QPS trace; Claire to confirm pilot stakeholders. We aim to kick off the pilot the week of 2025-06-02.
[08:35] Claire: Sounds good. Also send a list of the exact ports and peering requirements for VPC.
[08:40] Samir: Will do — I'll include the VPC runbook.
[08:44] Aisha: Curious about A/B: can we route 5% to a stronger reranker model?
[08:48] Samir: Yes — traffic splits are supported. You can do uplift tests and then ramp.
[08:53] Ben: Cool. Anything else?
[08:55] Jordan: We'll follow up with a single slide that maps architecture options to expected p95 and cost buckets, plus the benchmark plan.
[09:03] Claire: Thanks everyone. Looking forward to the benchmark numbers.
[09:06] (meeting ends)

Notes about transcript quality: several technical terms mangled by ASR (FAISS transcribed as "face's" on an earlier pass, KV cache came out as "K V cash" in places). Speaker labels mostly accurate.

References mentioned: SOC2, Pinecone, Milvus, FAISS, Redwood Optimize, Dedicated pools, VPC runbook (link to be sent).
